chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who prays two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer and does not sit in them, so he said: 'If he remembered while standing in the third rak'ah, let him sit; and if he did not remember until he bowed, let him complete his prayer, then prostrate two prostrations while sitting before he speaks.'

key_terms.يَجْلِسُ: he sits (referring to the sitting position in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to sit during the first two rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific fiqh of *sujud al-sahw* (prostration of forgetfulness) when a worshipper omits the sitting in the first two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer. It distinguishes between remembering while still standing in the third rak'ah, which requires sitting immediately, versus remembering after bowing, which necessitates completing the prayer and performing two seated prostrations before speaking. This highlights the Shia emphasis on precise ritual correction to maintain the validity of the prayer despite minor structural errors.
